title: The Voice: Four-Chair Turn Cade Mower Moves On After Battle Round
summary:
Cade Mower is still singing on The Voice. On Monday night, October 26, the 35-year-old singer from Bluffdale, Utah, advanced through the Battle round after performing the Red Clay Strays' Wondering Why with fellow Team Riley contestant Brayden Howell, who is 19.

Mower first turned all four chairs during the Blind Auditions with his performance of Zach Bryan's Something in the Orange. Coach Riley Green paired Mower and Howell for the Battle, with Carly Pearce joining Team Riley as a guest adviser. Before the performance, Mower spoke about the difficulty of being away from his wife, Lindsey, and their two children while filming the competition.

It's been a massive sacrifice, but if I can go and win this Battle, that's one step closer towards making this massive sacrifice worth it, he said. He added that his wife is not just along for the ride but his biggest fan. After the performance, Kelly Clarkson, who had been surprised during Mower's audition to learn that he works full-time as a wealth adviser, praised his voice.

Your vocals are insane, Clarkson told him. Queen Latifah said Mower had been on her brain since he came on the stage and wished he had landed on her team, while also praising Howell, telling the pair Brayden gave Mower a run for his money. Green ultimately selected Mower to advance, praising him for already knowing what he is and what he does well.

Mower has spent nearly 15 years pursuing music alongside a full-time career. According to NBC, he began playing guitar at age 12, started singing shortly before turning 21, and played thousands of shows while living in Austin and Nashville. The Battle win sends Mower into the newly introduced Cut Week as one of seven remaining artists on Team Riley.
why_it_matters: It shows that chasing a dream can take years of practice and big personal sacrifices, and that knowing your own strengths can help you stand out.
